races.name: Wexford Fillies Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Banner Beauty
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's charge has flat-code form over 8f that reads modestly (placed twice from six runs on Good) and steps up sharply in trip; a natural closer whose deep hold-up style is squeezed out by the similarly-minded field, meaning she is likely to race in a more prominent berth than suits her — style fit is materially compromised here.

runners_data.name: Casheldale Lass
runners_data.note: The race-shaper by default, Kinirons-trained and ridden by claiming jockey Smithers (7) off 27 days; her form shows a string of mid-pack finishes (8-12-8) and a tendency to fade, making it an open question whether she can sustain front-running duties over 2m1f despite being the only horse the map can place on the lead.

runners_data.name: Tell The Boys
runners_data.note: Queally's inmate arrives on the back of a form string that includes a win and a place at 2m on Good ground, and his trainer is in sharp form (3/7 over 14 days); the 61-day break is the one query, but his hold-up style may actually translate to a closer-to-pace role in a field this chaotic and his Good-ground record is the best of the confirmed types here.

runners_data.name: Baby Pearl
runners_data.note: De Bromhead second string ridden by Darragh O'Keeffe off a massive 245-day layoff; a single run over 17f on Heavy is all that exists and the step to Good ground introduces a genuine unknown alongside the fitness question — lightly raced flag is prominent and the fades-in-finish warning is a real concern for a horse returning after eight months.

runners_data.name: Ballyhahill
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's filly carries apprentice Williamson (5) and has shown modest form (best effort a 4th over 16f on Soft) with no Good-ground win on the board; a genuine back-marker by inclination, her natural position is crowded out in this field and she is likely to spend the race in a more forward berth than her jumping experience warrants over hurdles.

runners_data.name: Felicity Smoak
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's runner finished third at 20f on Good last time — her best effort — and prior form at shorter trips on Good showed little; a true rear-of-field type whose best chance is over a strong-run stamina test, but with the pace likely to be steady her hold-up role is devalued and the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 0/8 adds little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Kingside Lady
runners_data.note: McConnell's runner (0/25 over 14 days) has one run on record — a 13th over 17f on Good — and the fades-in-finish flag is a serious concern for a horse that has never shown she can see out a staying trip; 35 days fresh and carrying her natural hold-up instincts into a congested rear end means positional trouble is likely.

runners_data.name: Ribadora
runners_data.note: McCarthy's filly has four runs all on Good ground, recording consistent mid-division finishes between 5th and 7th — not spectacular but honest — over trips from 16f to 18f; 74 days since her last run is the primary concern, and she has no win on the card, but her familiarity with Good ground at this sort of distance makes her profile at least coherent for the conditions.

runners_data.name: Shakita
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins on Thomas Mullins's filly (0/5 in 14 days), wearing a hood and carrying a fades-in-finish warning; her form is poor across varying distances on Good and Soft and her redistribution into midfield from a true back-of-field position means she is likely to race in an unfamiliar location — hood first-time-over-hurdles factor is worth monitoring at the start.

runners_data.name: Sonas
runners_data.note: Debutant for De Bromhead (trainer in sharp form at 4/31 over 14 days) ridden by claiming rider Whelan (7) with no last-run data available — a complete unknown quantity; her going preference is unclassified and any pace-shape verdict around her is speculative, but De Bromhead fillies on debut over hurdles at Wexford deserve respect purely on trainer profile.

runners_data.name: Staywitherjohnny
runners_data.note: Murphy's filly (0/23 over 14 days) has five runs on record, all on Soft or Good-to-Soft in bumpers, with a best effort of 3rd over 8f on Good; this is a significant step up in trip and the surface has dried considerably compared to her preferred conditions — the trip and going combination is a dual concern heading into a 2m1f hurdle debut.

runners_data.name: Willows Word
runners_data.note: Rooney's debutant (trainer 0/1 over 14 days) wearing a hood on first appearance under rules; absolutely no form data to assess and going preference is entirely unknown — the hood suggests something to settle and the unknown profile makes her a pure wildcard who cannot be placed within any scenario with confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Casheldale Lass is the lone confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the front as the most likely race-shaper despite a natural hold-up tendency — she will set a measured, uncontested gallop over 2m1f on Good ground, creating a sustainable rhythm rather than a scorching tempo. With no genuine front-runner to challenge her, the pace will be controlled and honest rather than searching, meaning the race will be decided in the final two flights where stamina and jump accuracy matter most. The field is unusually hold-up heavy, with Banner Beauty, Ballyhahill, Felicity Smoak, and Shakita all true rear-of-field types redistributed into the midfield map because there is simply insufficient room at the back for all of them — in reality, those four will jostle for the same ground and few will secure their true position. This shape strongly favours a horse that can travel prominently in the slipstream of a controlled lead and produce a clean jump at the last, rather than a horse needing a strong pace to chase down from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Late Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Casheldale Lass sets a steady uncontested gallop and the winner swoops from a prominent position in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Casheldale Lass dictates at a fair clip with no rival pushing her, setting up a race won by whoever is closest to the pace and jumps the last fluently; prominent travelers are delivered into the race on their own terms without expending energy fighting for position early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Casheldale Lass, despite her hold-up tendencies, settles kindly and the strong pace-fearing field fails to mount a serious challenge.
scenarios.body: With a soft lead and a Good surface, Casheldale Lass could find a second wind at the second-last and the disorganised chasing pack — crammed with horses racing out of role — never coordinates a clean attack; a front-to-finish result becomes possible with this much positional chaos behind her.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Charge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the true hold-up horses manage to find daylight through the crowded midfield pack.
scenarios.body: Banner Beauty or Ballyhahill, if somehow able to carve a clear run, would benefit from a strong-run end-to-end gallop, but with so many hold-up types competing for the same late ground this scenario depends on fortunate gaps appearing at the right moment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Seizes Control
scenarios.trigger: If Casheldale Lass fails to hold the lead and an unraced or lightly raced unknown type takes over the front-running duties.
scenarios.body: Sonas or Willows Word, both debutants with entirely unknown profiles, could dictate an unplanned gallop if Casheldale Lass is taken off her feet early, rewriting the race shape entirely; this scenario is unlikely but non-zero given the number of unexposed runners in the field.

watchPoints.text: Casheldale Lass — watch whether she actually settles on the lead from flag-fall; if she idles or pulls hard in front the race shape collapses entirely and a chaotic mid-race scramble for the lead becomes likely with multiple hold-up horses suddenly out of position.

Ballyhahill and Shakita — both true hold-up types forced into mid-division, and with Williamson (5) and Danny Mullins fighting for the same ground approaching the first, a crowding incident in the early stages is a realistic risk that could unsettle several runners behind them.

Baby Pearl — 245 days off the track is a serious fitness concern for De Bromhead even in a stable in form; watch her in the paddock and early in the race for any sign she is not at peak fitness, as her fades-in-finish flag combined with a long absence is a compounding worry.

Sonas and Willows Word — both debutants from respected stables (De Bromhead and Rooney respectively), both wearing headgear; neither can be assessed from form but either could rewrite the pace map if they break sharp, particularly Sonas whose trainer has the best recent strike rate in the field.

Tell The Boys — Queally's 3/7 trainer form over 14 days is the standout stat in this race; watch whether Sexton elects to push him forward from his natural hold-up position given the likely lack of genuine early pace, as a prominent tactical ride could elevate his chance considerably.

races.name: Shamrock Farm Enterprises Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: It's Bobsled Time
runners_data.note: Trainer Declan Queally has two winners from seven runners in the past 14 days but this 4-year-old holds a poor sim-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 5 on Good) and carries a finish-fading flag — 182 days off and a cluttered recent form string (091F0) add further concern at this trip.

runners_data.name: Camino Rock
runners_data.note: Back quickly after a run 10 days ago, this 9-year-old has a modest sim-going record of 1W1P from 15 and has finished pulled-up or unplaced in recent outings; Josh Williamson's 5lb claim helps on the weights but the horse's best form was over shorter and on softer ground.

runners_data.name: Morell River
runners_data.note: Colin Bowe's 6-year-old owns the most compelling Good-ground form in the field (2W3P from 11 similar runs) and showed a useful second at 2m4f on Good last time; though the race map places it in midfield due to runner redistribution, it is a genuine hold-up type that will naturally race in behind before making its move late, and its OR of 102 gives it a meaningful class edge.

runners_data.name: Harpy Eagle
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in this field, Paddy Cody's mount for R P Cody will lead from the outset and set a sustainable pace on Good ground; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) signals a modest positional edge and it has form in the frame on Good going (3 places from 12), though it has not won in nine tries on this surface.

runners_data.name: Marian Avenue
runners_data.note: C Byrnes's 6-year-old carries a finish-fading flag and a weak Good-ground record (0W1P from 7), and 72 days off the track adds a fitness question; despite the midfield map position due to redistribution, it is a genuine hold-up horse whose recent form — a second at 2m — is the sole bright note.

runners_data.name: Ocean Murphy
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe partners this interesting 4-year-old who won at 2m on Good ground last season and wears a hood; naturally a hold-up horse pushed into midfield on the map by redistribution, its OR of 98 and limited sim-going record (1W1P from 7) suggest it is competitive without being the obvious dominant force.

runners_data.name: Isdistheone
runners_data.note: The big weight concession (147lbs) and a 90-day absence make life hard for Kevin Healy (7lb claim) and trainer Declan Queally's second runner; a tongue-tie is applied and the sim-going record (0W0P from 10 on Good) gives little encouragement, while the redistribution map places this true hold-up horse in midfield — it is the lowest-rated runner here.

races.paceDynamic: Harpy Eagle is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate from the outset on Good ground over 2m4f, setting a sustainable rather than pressured gallop with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead. The remainder of the field — It's Bobsled Time, Camino Rock, Morell River, Marian Avenue, Ocean Murphy, and Isdistheone — are all hold-up types by nature, meaning the pace will be modest and the race will compress into a steadily-run contest that sets up a late sprint rather than a stamina test. This shape classically favours horses who can travel smoothly in behind and produce a clean, sharp finish, though the Good ground and lack of pressure on the leader also means Harpy Eagle could simply control the tempo and steal a march on a flat-to-finish field. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can place at the rear; Morell River, Marian Avenue, and Ocean Murphy are true hold-up horses forced into midfield roles on the map, and in reality they will race as a bunch behind the leader — Morell River, with the best recent form on Good ground, and Ocean Murphy, who has won at this trip on this surface, are most likely to secure the prominent positions directly behind Harpy Eagle. The race shape most favours a horse that can travel close enough to Harpy Eagle to pounce in the final flight and home straight without being caught flat-footed from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Harpy Eagle Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Harpy Eagle bowls along in front at a comfortable clip and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Harpy Eagle controls every yard of the race on a modest pace, using the lack of any rival front-runner to build a winning advantage into the home straight; the hold-up horses, forced to make up ground from a standing gallop, find the task too great on flat Good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that the hold-up pack travel within striking distance throughout and the best finisher wins a sprint.
scenarios.body: Morell River or Ocean Murphy, both genuine hold-up types with solid form on Good going, track close enough to Harpy Eagle and produce the sharpest late kick; the compressed finish suits horses with a turn of foot rather than those who fade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Collared On Line
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent-tracking horse latches onto Harpy Eagle early and the pair grind each other into a slow final furlong, gifting a late closer.
scenarios.body: Harpy Eagle finds a rival tracking too close for comfort, the pair burn each other out approaching the last, and a fresher hold-up type swoops to collar them close home; Morell River's good-ground two-mile-plus form makes it the chief threat in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Thins Field
scenarios.trigger: If the Good ground rides more testing than forecast and errors or fatigue thin the runners, producing a race of attrition.
scenarios.body: A grinding test exposes runners with jumping or stamina questions — Harpy Eagle's consistent prominent-style placing record on Good gives it resilience, while Camino Rock's experience over further on similar ground becomes relevant; hold-up horses who fade in finish, flagged for It's Bobsled Time and Marian Avenue, are vulnerable.

watchPoints.text: Morell River's Good-ground form (2W3P from 11 similar runs) stands out sharply — watch whether it travels fluently in the pocket behind Harpy Eagle and makes smooth headway from two out.

Harpy Eagle sets the pace alone but its STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) and winless record in 9 attempts on Good suggest it could be caught flat-footed if it fails to build enough of a cushion before the home straight.

It's Bobsled Time and Marian Avenue both carry a finish-fading flag — watch for either weakening sharply from the second-last flight, which would confirm the pace dynamic is playing against hold-up types who cannot sustain their effort.

Ocean Murphy wears a hood and is returning on a quick 16-day turnaround — watch for any signs of freshness or keenness early that could compromise its natural hold-up position, particularly behind a lone front-runner going a modest gallop.

Camino Rock's trainer has only one runner in the 14-day window with no winners — monitor market moves late, as this 9-year-old at OR 104 on a quick return could be a forgotten handicap-savvy type if money arrives.

races.name: Wexford Racecourse Park Run Beginners Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Begger
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse trained by William Harvey who has struggled for a clear finishing effort recently, showing a pattern of fading in the finish across three runs on Good; the 11-day turnaround is short and the form string (U5-U70) inspires little confidence over this trip.

runners_data.name: Jackson Lamb
runners_data.note: John C McConnell's seven-year-old is a natural prominent racer with genuine claims here, boasting three wins from 13 starts on similar Good ground and a course win at the right distance; headgear (p) has been worn before and Alex Harvey takes the ride for a yard that is 0/25 in the past 14 days, which is a note of caution.

runners_data.name: Nadia's Boy
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes over for Willie Mullins, who is 16/62 in the past fortnight, and this six-year-old is the race's sole confirmed front-runner with two recent wins on Good ground; his 39-day break is not a concern given the stable's record, and he holds all the tactical cards from the front.

runners_data.name: Scalpnagoon
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old is a consistent prominent performer who has finished second or third five times from 14 Good-ground starts without winning, suggesting a pattern of finding one too good; the tongue-tie is retained and Josh Williamson claims 5lb, which could be an advantage if the novice field makes jumping errors.

runners_data.name: West Away
runners_data.note: P E Collins's eight-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — pushed to the midfield slot on this map because the field lacks space at the rear — meaning his style fit is compromised (0.92 discount) and his chance is tempered by racing in an unnatural position; only one win from 15 Good-ground starts and the 17-day turnaround is unremarkable.

runners_data.name: William Tell
runners_data.note: A prominent-type on paper but the form string (-972U5) is alarming for a beginners' chase, with an unseating and repeated mid-field finishes; tongue-tie is fitted and the 7lb claim for Peter Smithers is a factor, but David Harry Kelly's 0/6 in the past 14 days is noted.

runners_data.name: Kelya
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins's six-year-old carries a featherweight (159lbs) and showed ability when placed in earlier form, but returns from a significant layoff of 513 days — the longest absence in the field — with only two runs on similar ground (1/2) offering limited evidence; Donagh Meyler rides and the horse must be treated as a genuine unknown over fences.

races.paceDynamic: Nadia's Boy (Paul Townend, W P Mullins) is the lone confirmed front-runner in a seven-runner beginners' chase and will dictate from the front unchallenged, setting a sustainable, controlling gallop over 2m3f on Good ground at Wexford. Jackson Lamb and Scalpnagoon are the natural prominent types who will track Nadia's Boy at close quarters, while William Tell has prominent form but a patchy recent record that makes him a less reliable presence near the pace. The hold-up brigade — Begger, Kelya, and West Away — will operate from the rear, though West Away is a genuine prominent type redistributed to midfield on this map because the field holds more hold-up horses than the shape can accommodate at the back; Nadia's Boy and Jackson Lamb are most likely to actually secure their natural positions. A single uncontested front-runner over this trip on Good ground creates a measured, confidence-building pace that strongly favours prominent horses with the tactical speed to sit on the leader's back and pounce, rather than deep hold-up types who face a stamina-sapping closing burst from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nadia's Boy Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Nadia's Boy bowls along unchallenged and sets a true but unhurried gallop that suits prominent chasers.
scenarios.body: Nadia's Boy dictates fully on his own terms, with Jackson Lamb and Scalpnagoon travelling into the race in his wake before the front three fight it out from two out; the Good ground and relatively modest pace rewards horses who have been in the race throughout. Prominent types who travel and jump fluently are in the best position to capitalise if the leader has a chink, and Scalpnagoon's repeated placed efforts at this level make him the likeliest beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Nadia's Boy hits a flat spot or a jumping error late and Jackson Lamb or Scalpnagoon pick him off from the last.
scenarios.body: The race unfolds as above but a tired jump or mistake from the leader hands the initiative to whichever prominent horse has travelled best; Jackson Lamb's sole course win on Good going and Scalpnagoon's consistent placed record both give them the profile to capitalise quickly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Nadia's Boy goes too hard in front and the race falls apart, allowing a closer to finish through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: A true beginner's-chase novice pace implosion opens the door for Begger or Kelya to finish strongly into a weakening field; however, both are lightly exposed over fences and Kelya returns from 513 days off the track, which limits confidence in this shape materialising with conviction.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls To Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, fallers, or a chaotic early gallop disrupt the expected order and produce an unusually open finish.
scenarios.body: In a beginners' steeplechase on Good ground with seven runners including novices, a cluster of errors can compress the field and hand an advantage to whichever horse jumps most fluently and avoids trouble; William Tell's recent form (U among recent figures) highlights the fallibility in the line-up.

watchPoints.text: Watch Nadia's Boy's jumping from the front — if Paul Townend's mount makes a significant error at a fence, the entire race dynamic collapses and Scalpnagoon or Jackson Lamb will be immediate beneficiaries.

Kelya's 513-day absence is a significant risk factor; a horse returning from that length of layoff in a beginners' steeplechase can be unpredictable and may cause interference if it makes a jumping error in the pack.

West Away is a natural hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to the field's composition — monitor whether Patrick O'Brien pushes for a more forward position than the horse's natural running style warrants, as this could affect the midfield picture for Scalpnagoon and Jackson Lamb.

William Tell's recent unseating (U in form string) is relevant in a beginners' chase context — a repeat jumping error could affect runners immediately behind him and deserves pre-race positional awareness.

Trainer strike rates tell a story in this race: Mullins (T14: 16/62) contrasts sharply with Elliott (1/43) and McConnell (0/25), which reinforces the case that Nadia's Boy carries the strongest stable momentum into this contest.

races.name: Wexfordraces.ie Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Leave In Secret
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner, clear style advantage here as the unchallenged pace-setter; Thomas Gibney's runner has consistent good-ground form (sim-going 12/15) and has placed twice in five runs at 2m-plus trips, though a topweight of 166lbs and recent form reading 67-743 raises a stamina-in-closing query — James Smith's 5lb claim partially offsets the weight burden.

runners_data.name: Freddie Robdal
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's nine-year-old returns off 56 days and carries a strong each-way profile — two second-place finishes at this trip and going band in recent history — and Danny Power's 7lb claim is a meaningful handicap asset; class hold-up horse whose style ideally suits waiting off a single pace-setter.

runners_data.name: Beggars Rock
runners_data.note: Ran just six days ago which demands attention for freshness; Ian Patrick Donoghue's 0/8 trainer strike rate over 14 days is a negative flag, and recent form shows finishes of P63-60, but the horse has placed at 26f on good and has experience over trips longer than today's 2m3f.

runners_data.name: Tequila Talkin'
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan's seven-year-old has placed twice at the 2m-2m2f range on good ground and ran third 17 days ago, suggesting reasonable fitness; Carl Millar's 5lb claim helps in the handicap and headgear listed as hood (hg:h) may sharpen focus, making this an each-way profile if the pace sets up for a single late run.

runners_data.name: Centreofattention
runners_data.note: Ed Bolger's runner showed a placed second last time over 2m on good ground, indicating live form on the going; a natural hold-up horse whose position on the map does not reflect how he will likely race — expect him to settle at the rear regardless — and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence that he can produce a winning run from further back than ideal.

runners_data.name: Oneforgonzo
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on good 10 days ago which confirms fitness and going suitability, but the horse's natural settling tendency means he may find himself covering extra ground from the rear in a race where the pace will not be breakneck; Anna McGuinness's 7lb claim is a positive, though Sean Aherne's 0/1 recent trainer record is a thin sample.

runners_data.name: Temptationinmilan
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old carrying 150lbs with a form string of 450-7P and a trainer who has 0/0 recent runners — this profile requires a significant upturn in form; genuine hold-up horse who will settle deep by instinct, but Wexford's sharp layout and good ground historically have not produced wins for this horse (0W0P in sim-going sample).

runners_data.name: Following Orders
runners_data.note: Prominent type who slots behind Leave In Secret logically, but recent form of 5P-09P is deeply uninspiring and the trainer P J Rothwell's 0/18 strike rate over 14 days is the most significant negative flag in the field; blinkers (hg:b) suggest connections are seeking a behavioural improvement, but the six-year-old has not placed in 11 similar-going runs.

runners_data.name: Avec Espoir
runners_data.note: Aged 13 and returning from a 307-day absence — the longest layoff in the field — with a form string of /0P00-; V T O'Brien's runner has course experience but all recent runs show double-digit finishes or pulled-up, and it is very difficult to construct a scenario in which a 13-year-old back after nearly a year off at OR 89 wins this race.

races.paceDynamic: Leave In Secret is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to contest the lead, should dictate from the off at a sustainable gallop on good ground over 2m3f at Wexford. Following Orders and Avec Espoir are both prominent types who may attempt to press early but neither has the profile to truly challenge for the front, meaning Leave In Secret should settle into a rhythm unchallenged. The field behind is dominated by hold-up horses — Freddie Robdal, Beggars Rock, Tequila Talkin', Centreofattention, Oneforgonzo, and Temptationinmilan — creating a scenario where closers must produce late runs from a compressed midfield-to-rear group. This race shape — a controlled, uncontested gallop set by one horse — strongly favours genuine hold-up horses who can travel through and produce a single sustained run in the straight, provided they have the scope to cover ground from off the pace; horses who jump fluently and stay in touch without expending energy are at a premium. Centreofattention, Oneforgonzo, and Temptationinmilan are all true hold-up types redistributed forward on the map because there are more rear-runners than positions — in reality they are all likely to settle at the back, and only those who can produce a powerful finish from deep will get involved.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leave In Secret Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Leave In Secret bowls along unchallenged and the closers leave their runs too late on a sound Wexford surface.
scenarios.body: Leave In Secret sets a measured gallop, racks up the fences on good ground, and the chasing pack fails to close the gap through the final two fences; the horse's jumping efficiency is the weapon and Thomas Gibney's runner exploits the vacuum in the pace. Prominent types Following Orders or Avec Espoir who sit just behind may find themselves second-best but staying on, while the hold-up brigade run out of real estate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely moderate and one of the true closers — Freddie Robdal or Beggars Rock — travels powerfully and arrives with a late run that catches Leave In Secret.
scenarios.body: A measured gallop can actually allow the better-quality hold-up horse to travel sweetly in behind and pounce from the second-last; Freddie Robdal's two recent second-placed runs over shorter trips on similar ground suggest he retains class at this level, and Danny Power (claiming 7lb) is an asset in a handicap. Beggars Rock has course-distance form on good and his trainer's recent 0/8 strike rate is a flag, but the horse's profile at this trip suits the scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Gatecrashes
scenarios.trigger: If Following Orders or Avec Espoir attach themselves to Leave In Secret and a two-horse lead group builds momentum that Leave In Secret cannot sustain alone.
scenarios.body: Leave In Secret gets company it did not bargain for and the pace becomes genuinely contested, causing both leaders to flatten out at the final fence; a prominent-to-midfield horse sitting just off the pace — Tequila Talkin' or Centreofattention, who has winning form over this sort of trip on good — could then emerge with a fresher finish. Tequila Talkin' has shown a liking for good ground and has placed at this trip previously, making her a candidate here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp The Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically at the last and multiple hold-up horses arrive together, with Oneforgonzo or Temptationinmilan involved.
scenarios.body: This requires a near-total collapse of front-running stamina AND a perfectly-timed late run from the back-markers, which is the least likely combination given the controlled nature of the anticipated gallop. Oneforgonzo has a recent Goodwood-going win over 20f and Temptationinmilan has a respectable profile on good ground, but neither has convincing form at this level and both carry STYLE_FIT concerns after being pushed out of their natural position.

watchPoints.text: Leave In Secret is the unchallenged pace-setter and if James Smith settles the horse fluently over the early fences, the entire field is chasing a horse that has controlled its own energy — watch for the gap failing to close from the second-last.

Freddie Robdal returns off 56 days for Henry De Bromhead — watch his jumping sharpness in the early stages, as a rusty jumper off a layoff can lose momentum quickly at Wexford's compact fences, costing him the clean run his profile demands.

Following Orders carries blinkers and a dire recent form string (5P-09P) alongside the worst trainer strike rate in the field (0/18 over 14 days) — watch for an early exit or pull-up that disrupts the midfield pack if he jumps poorly behind Leave In Secret.

Beggars Rock races for the second time in six days — watch whether he shows signs of residual fatigue in the closing stages, particularly given a trainer who has not scored recently; if he fades tamely from the second-last it will confirm the quick turnaround took its toll.

Avec Espoir's 307-day absence makes him a potential jumping hazard at pace on good ground — watch his jumping at the first two fences, as a blunder or early departure could unsettle horses travelling immediately behind him.

races.name: Poolcourt Engineering Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Sphagnum
runners_data.note: Consistent performer on Good ground (12/15 similar-going record) but has not won for a while, and with the field's pace bias likely to force him to race more prominently than usual, his stamina over this 3m1f trip will be tested; the 7lb claimer Mr J P Sampson is a factor to weigh up in a competitive heat.

runners_data.name: Rockonliam
runners_data.note: Back-to-back winners and the most credible front-runner in the field, stepping up sharply in trip from 2m4f to 3m1f for the first time, which is the key query — De Bromhead's yard is in form (4/31 T14) and Darragh O'Keeffe's booking is a clear positive, but whether he stays this far on a day he must likely race hard from the front is the crux.

runners_data.name: Jacovec Cavern
runners_data.note: Travelled from a wide-open mark (OR 116) with solid Good-ground form including a recent win over 2m7f, and the 5lb claim from Richard Condon keeps the weight manageable; a prominent racer by nature who should find a comfortable position just behind the two leaders in this shape.

runners_data.name: Rue Taylor
runners_data.note: Won over 2m7f in Good ground on his latest outing and is on a workable mark, with the 5lb claimer Eoin Staples easing the burden; Paul Nolan's yard is 0/8 in the past 14 days which warrants a note, but the horse's form profile suits a strongly-run staying chase where prominent runners can stay on.

runners_data.name: Teenage Kiss
runners_data.note: Won last time out and is clearly in good heart for Conor O'Dwyer's in-form yard (3/4 T14), but in truth races prominently by nature and is mapped to midfield here purely because two genuine front-runners occupy that space ahead of him — his chance may be tempered by not getting a position that suits, though his recent win gives him a solid claim if he can settle further back than usual.

runners_data.name: Ceroc
runners_data.note: Returned to winning form 17 days ago and arrives fresh, but has a modest sim-going record (11/15, 1 win) and the key concern is whether he can sustain his front-running role over this markedly longer 3m1f trip against a rival (Rockonliam) equally determined to lead; if he is outgunned for the lead he may find his race falling apart quickly.

runners_data.name: Duty Bound
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer placed at the rear on the pace map only because the field is light on true hold-up types, meaning his tactical position in this race is unlikely to be as deep as shown; with a P5 recent form line and a 39-day absence, he faces a stern task on what is a modest current mark, and his chance in any shape requiring him to come from the back is discounted accordingly.

races.paceDynamic: Rockonliam and Ceroc are the two confirmed front-runners in this seven-runner staying chase over 3m1f on Good ground at Wexford, and with both handlers likely to allow their horses to bowl along in front, a genuinely contested early pace is the most probable race shape. Rockonliam brings strong recent form (two consecutive wins) and is handled by Darragh O'Keeffe for the in-form De Bromhead yard, while Ceroc returned to winning form 17 days ago and has Philip Enright aboard — neither side is likely to concede the lead meekly, creating an honest, attritional gallop that will stretch the field from the front. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Rockonliam and Ceroc are most likely to actually lead, with Sphagnum, Jacovec Cavern, and Rue Taylor likely pushed to just off the pace, and Teenage Kiss and Duty Bound — both true prominent racers — redistributed further back than ideal. A race run at a genuine clip over this staying trip on Good ground heavily favours prominent-to-patient chasers who travel economically behind the speed and conserve energy for the final circuit, rather than true hold-up types or those who must use excess energy duelling for position early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Rockonliam and Ceroc fight for supremacy and set a genuine gallop, burning off the field before the home turn.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a demanding pace that stretches the field, with the race becoming a stamina examination from three out; horses that sit just off the pace in a prominent position without expending early energy are best placed to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of Rockonliam or Ceroc outpaces the other early and the race settles into a controlled lead.
scenarios.body: A single horse controls matters from the front at a measured tempo, making it a test of class and jumping rather than raw stamina; a well-handicapped front-runner dictating their own rhythm and jumping fluently is the chief beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fade, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace causes Rockonliam and Ceroc to tie up late and horses from behind come with a sustained run.
scenarios.body: The front-runners exhaust themselves, opening the door for the prominent horses just behind the pace — Sphagnum or Rue Taylor — to reel them in up the straight; this scenario suits horses that settled in the first third of the field without expending early energy.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: False Pace, Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is deceptive and collapses late, allowing hold-up types to swoop from the rear.
scenarios.body: This shape depends largely on Duty Bound and Teenage Kiss, both of whom are natural prominent types mapped rearward due to redistribution, meaning they are not genuine hold-up horses and this scenario is the least likely to deliver; even if it materialises, the lack of a true closer makes a bold challenge from the rear improbable.

watchPoints.text: Rockonliam and Ceroc are on a collision course for the lead — watch whether either jockey concedes or whether they force a burning pace that plays into the hands of Jacovec Cavern or Rue Taylor sitting just behind.

Rockonliam has not raced beyond 2m4f in any of his last five starts — the step to 3m1f while being pushed for the lead by Ceroc is an unproven stamina combination that could see him empty after the fourth-last.

Teenage Kiss and Duty Bound are both natural front-of-the-field horses displaced rearward by the map — if either settles poorly or uses energy scrambling for position in the first mile, their chances are effectively compromised before the race has really begun.

The Good ground is consistent across all Wexford races today, so no horse faces an unexpected surface shift, but the 3m1f trip is the longest on the card and the pace battle up front may make sectionals significantly quicker in the first half than comparable handicap chases over shorter.

Henry De Bromhead's yard is showing a solid 4/31 T14 strike rate, and Darragh O'Keeffe's booking for Rockonliam stands out as a significant positive in what is otherwise a competitive lower-grade handicap chase.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Solsbury Hill
runners_data.note: Conor O'Dwyer's seven-year-old has strong Good-ground claims (11 runs on similar going, two wins and three places) and returns after 39 days off in good order; apprentice Charlie O'Dwyer takes the ride on a confirmed hold-up horse who needs the gallop to be honest enough to make late ground on a sharp Wexford circuit.

runners_data.name: Bynx
runners_data.note: Consistent profile on Good going with 13 runs and three wins at the trip range, and Sam Ewing is an experienced pilot, but this hold-up horse will need things to unfold in front of him on a sharp 1m7½f track where off-the-pace tactics are structurally disadvantaged today.

runners_data.name: Ned In The Park
runners_data.note: The race's only true front-runner, he has the role to himself and will control the tempo, which is the single most important tactical factor here; the STYLE_FIT flag is noted given his preferred stamina trips of 2m+, and the 11-day turnaround on a sharp, shorter track is worth monitoring for jumping focus.

runners_data.name: Lady Doyanne
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's six-year-old has useful form (1W3P from 7 runs on similar going) and Darragh O'Keeffe is a high-class booking, but she is a genuine hold-up horse by nature who finds herself mapped to midfield because the rear is congested — her STYLE_FIT flag reflects that she is unlikely to secure her preferred position and the short trip constrains her further.

runners_data.name: Kilbrin Rocco
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Good going and has prominent-style form that makes him naturally suited to tracking the leader today; the 11-day turnaround is tight, but trainer McCarthy has recent track activity and a tongue-tie is fitted — he is one of the two horses most structurally suited to the race shape this day produces.

runners_data.name: Ballybrittas
runners_data.note: A two-time winner on Good ground over this trip range and PJ Rothwell's 17-day freshener is standard, but Ballybrittas is a hold-up horse by inclination whose natural rear position is already taken by others — shown in midfield on the map but unlikely to be comfortable there, with the STYLE_FIT flag appropriately dampening expectations.

runners_data.name: Rightfolksplease
runners_data.note: Kevin Healy claims 7lbs for Declan Queally and the horse has a win and a placed effort over 16f on Good; a tongue-tie is in place and the prominent profile fits today's shape well, though the F in recent form and an 0 make jumping reliability the key question to answer on the day.

races.paceDynamic: Ned In The Park is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner novice chase over an extended mile-and-seven furlongs, and with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, he will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset. Behind him, Kilbrin Rocco and Rightfolksplease will push for prominent positions, giving the race a clear three-tier structure: leader, prominent pair, and a rear group. The field holds more hold-up types than the race map can place at the back — Lady Doyanne and Ballybrittas are natural hold-up horses who are shown in midfield simply because the rear is crowded with similar profiles, and both will struggle to get the true off-the-pace position they prefer. This sustainable, uncontested pace on Good ground over a sharp 1m7½f trip strongly favours horses who travel prominently and stay in touch, rewarding Prominent-to-Lead profiles rather than pure closers who will find the tempo insufficient to generate the gaps they need late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ned Dictates, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Ned In The Park goes unchallenged to the front and sets a measured, controlled pace that rewards those racing in his slipstream.
scenarios.body: Ned In The Park establishes a comfortable rhythm and the race is run at a tempo that suits horses prominent from the start, with Kilbrin Rocco and Rightfolksplease the two most likely to pick up the pieces if the leader tires at the final obstacles. Hold-up horses are left with too little to aim at off a moderate gallop on a sharp track.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Ned In The Park's early pace is fractionally stronger than expected and the prominent pair use themselves up chasing him, leaving hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: Solsbury Hill and Bynx, both holding strong recent form on Good ground, have the class and finishing reserves to make up ground if the race develops any late drop in tempo. Their Go-OK profiles and similar-going records give them each a plausible closing chance, though the track's sharpness limits the opportunity.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Bolts Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Ned In The Park, racing off just an 11-day break and on a sharp track, pings his fences and builds a commanding lead that proves unassailable.
scenarios.body: Riding as a 7lb claimer, Mr D Doyle has little pressure from rivals and could exploit the situation if Ned jumps cleanly throughout; the short-run-in at Wexford means any lead entering the home straight is difficult to peg back. The prominent horses are then competing for places rather than the prize.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Creates Opportunity
scenarios.trigger: If there are jumping errors or fallers among the front group that reshuffle the race entirely.
scenarios.body: With Ned In The Park holding a U in recent form and Rightfolksplease carrying an F in his string, jumping reliability is a genuine concern and a chaotic mid-race incident could allow survivors from any position to benefit. Lady Doyanne and Ballybrittas, forced out of their natural hold-up roles, could find themselves accidentally well-placed if the front brigade causes trouble.

watchPoints.text: Ned In The Park carries a U in recent form — watch his jumping closely from the first fence, as a mistake or exit by the sole pace-setter would completely reshape the race for all seven runners.
Rightfolksplease has both an F and a 0 in his recent string, making him a jumping risk when pressed from a prominent position; if he falls or blunders early, the field directly behind him is at risk.

Lady Doyanne and Ballybrittas are both natural hold-up horses forced towards midfield today — watch whether either can find a settling position early, because if both push forward instinctively the tactical integrity of the mid-group could break down.

The 1m7½f Wexford chase trip is on the sharp side for several of these horses who have predominant form at 2m+; watch for any signs of horses being asked to quicken before they are truly comfortable in the straight.

Trainer Conor O'Dwyer has sent Solsbury Hill out after 39 days off with a 3/4 recent strike-rate — watch the market moves on the hold-up horse, as support would signal stable confidence that the return is timed perfectly.
